blocks.text: Deer Lake Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Deer Lake houses ring a park, not a shopping street: Deer Lake Park at 6450 Deer Lake Avenue is the centre, and the City calls the park the cultural centre of Burnaby.
Deer Lake Avenue carries the institutions: the Shadbolt Centre for the Arts and Burnaby Village Museum parking lots are both accessed from Deer Lake Avenue.
Sperling Avenue is the west-side working street: the City's boardwalk detour runs walkers onto Sperling Avenue and Deer Lake Drive, about five extra minutes of walking.

blocks.text: Deer Lake Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Houses here sit against park zoning: the Official Zoning Map in the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 shows Deer Lake Avenue parcels in R1, P1 and P2 districts beside the lake.
The built landmark stock is institutional, not strata: Burnaby Village Museum at 6501 Deer Lake Avenue and the Shadbolt Centre at 6450 Deer Lake Avenue anchor the north shore.
The City treats Deer Lake as an Urban Village in its form and character guidelines, listed with Burnaby Mountain, Montecito and East Burnaby.

blocks.text: Deer Lake Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Park hours shape the streets: Deer Lake Park is open from dawn until dusk year-round, so the lake roads carry event and visitor traffic in daylight hours only.
Zoning is read on the Official Zoning Map at 1:1000 scale under the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, and a boundary following a road allowance or creek is read from that map, not from a listing.
Form and character review can apply in the Deer Lake Urban Village: the Zoning Bylaw No. 14815 guidelines name Deer Lake among the Urban Villages meant to support walkable, mixed development forms.

blocks.text: Deer Lake Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The boardwalk by the boat launch is being fully replaced: that section closed beginning September 21, with completion scheduled by winter 2027 and a signed detour via Sperling Avenue.
The City monitors waterway health at Deer Lake with the Pacific Streamkeepers, a volunteer organization working on watershed education and clean-ups.
BC Spirits Square, built in 2010 beside the Shadbolt Centre, holds the City's first piece of public art: carved stone monoliths by Coast Salish artist Thomas Cannell.
The Shadbolt building won the Canadian Wood Council Award of Merit in 1996 for its creative wood and stone design.
The City's film kit lists Deer Lake Park and the Shadbolt Centre among Burnaby's popular filming locations, which explains periodic production closures on Deer Lake Avenue.

blocks.text: Deer Lake Houses: development and new projects

items.t: Deer Lake Park boardwalk replacement, boat launch area on Deer Lake Avenue, City of Burnaby, boardwalk structure replacement with picnic area section closed during work. Status: closed from September 21, completion scheduled by winter 2027 (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Deer Lake Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: Culture here is City-funded, not strata-funded: the Shadbolt Centre, Burnaby Art Gallery and Burnaby Village Museum are owned or operated by the City, and the museum's admission is free.
Walking is the local system: leisurely trails connect the lake, the Burnaby Art Gallery, the Shadbolt Centre, Burnaby Village Museum and Hart House restaurant inside one park network.
Deer Lake Avenue now carries a multi-use pathway from the City's completed improvement project, separating park walkers from the Deer Lake Drive traffic.
During the boardwalk work, the signed walking detour adds about five minutes via Sperling Avenue and Deer Lake Drive.

blocks.text: Deer Lake Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check event load on Deer Lake Avenue before assuming quiet: the Festival Lawn hosts concerts and festivals overlooking the lake, in the heart of the arts precinct.
Check the zoning map sheet for the exact lot: Deer Lake Avenue parcels split between R1 housing, P1 park and P2 institutional districts on the Official Zoning Map.

blocks.text: Deer Lake home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

5 houses sold in Deer Lake with a median price of $2,900,000, taking a median of 24 days to sell at 93.0% of the last list price; 20% sold above list. They had a median $717 per square foot, a median year built of 1990 and a median lot of 13,090 square feet.

A figure is shown only where at least 5 homes sold, and a row is shown only with 5 or more sales; with fewer, one sale would be the whole figure.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Deer Lake?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 16 houses listed in Deer Lake. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Deer Lake a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses in Deer Lake had no published sales ratio for the month. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many houses sold in Deer Lake from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 3 houses sold in Deer Lake over those 5 months, out of 251 in all of Burnaby.

faq.q: Does this page include townhomes or duplexes in Deer Lake?
faq.a: No. The figures are for detached houses only. Condos and townhomes are counted on their own page.

faq.q: What did houses in Deer Lake sell for?
faq.a: 5 houses sold in Deer Lake between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $2,900,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Deer Lake?
faq.a: The median was 24 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 93.0% of the last list price (20% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
